speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, particularly the nature of the facial grimacing? Do you or any witnesses notice any rhythmic movements or loss of muscle tone during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does anyone notice if he has an aura, such as the muddy taste you mentioned, before every episode, and are there any other strange smells, sounds, or feelings he describes? Also, does he have a history of seizures or any recent head injuries?

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: EEG. Do the episodes occur more frequently during sleep or when he is awake, and has anyone noticed any tongue biting or incontinence during these events?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram (EEG): Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side. Note: Information regarding the frequency of episodes during sleep vs. awake, tongue biting, or incontinence is not available in the provided test data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG showing temporal lobe spikes strongly suggests focal seizures, likely with an olfactory aura given the "muddy taste." To better characterize the seizure focus and rule out a structural cause like a tumor or lesion, I need to see the brain's anatomy. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the EEG findings of right temporal spikes and the specific aura described, I am fairly confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
